picks.excerpt: Figma argues that AI accelerates execution but not clarity, so teams increasingly mistake polished AI output for a sound decision. It lays out the context layers — design systems, a stated point of view, explicit constraints — that keep fast AI work pointed at the right problem instead of generating tech debt.
picks.rationale: First-party Figma guidance that a design team can apply tomorrow: name the context layers before letting agents run, so speed does not turn into tech debt.

picks.excerpt: zeroheight details the Design System Documentation Spec now moving through the W3C, aiming to standardise how component docs are structured across tools. A shared machine-readable doc format is the missing half of design tokens for AI-driven handoff.
picks.rationale: A real standards move at the W3C — the documentation counterpart to design tokens, and the thing that decides whether agents can read a design system at all.

picks.excerpt: A practical UX framework for deciding where an AI feature physically lives in a product — floating widget, inline assist, sidebar or a dedicated hub. The argument is that placement, not model quality, determines whether users discover, trust and keep using the AI.
picks.rationale: Concrete placement patterns for AI features — the decision most product designers are actually making this week, framed as a UX problem rather than a model problem. Second card in the figma category, so it takes a distinct palette accent.

picks.excerpt: Google is adding a toggle that removes the visible sparkle watermark from images and video made with its Nano Banana, Omni and Lyria models, while invisible SynthID marks and C2PA metadata stay attached. It changes what AI-generated creative assets look like when they ship into client work.
picks.rationale: Newest item in the pool and it directly changes deliverables: generated assets can now ship without the visible sparkle, while the invisible provenance marks stay.

picks.excerpt: Vercel's AI SDK harness layer now works with any Agent Client Protocol (ACP)-compatible harness through the new @ai-sdk/harness-acp package. Instead of wrapping one runtime per adapter — Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Deep Agents, OpenCode — it wraps the protocol, so a design-engineering team can point HarnessAgent at any harness that ships an ACP package.
picks.rationale: A meta adapter that decouples agent workflows from a single vendor runtime — design-engineering teams can swap the harness behind their design-to-code agents without rewriting the integration.
